title: The practices, looking back
hook: prayer, sabbath, scripture, giving, fasting, song
tomorrow: why would a gospel end with people too scared to talk?

segments.voice: A week from near the top, in six lines: a rule for love; the last climb; stories still working; keep it in your heart; the week that turned the world; and yesterday, the story reached here. Today, the habits that carried all of it.
screen: `SIX LINES FROM THE TOP.` → `THE STORY REACHED HERE.` → `NOW, THE HABITS.`

segments.voice: A gym membership, a language-app streak, a journal with three pages filled in: good starts pile up. This path has offered six old practices: prayer, a day of rest, scripture, giving, fasting, song. Some found room in an ordinary week and kept it. Some lasted a few days and slipped away. Both tell you something. So, which one stayed?
screen: `GOOD STARTS PILE UP.` → `PRAYER, REST, A PAGE, A GIFT, A FAST, A SONG.` → `WHICH ONE STAYED?`

segments.voice: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus talks about giving, prayer and fasting in a row, and the grammar is the thing to tell a friend: he says when, not if. “But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth.” “But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet.” And a fast that doesn't show: “But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face.” Each one done quietly, each one assumed, part of an ordinary week rather than a trophy. The sabbath gets the same gentleness in Mark: “The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.” A practice serves the person, not the other way round, so it can bend when a life changes shape. And Paul gives scripture and song one line: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly.” Dwell means live there. Move in. Unpack. That may be the real test of a practice: not how hard it was tried in the first week, but whether it moved in. Looking back, the one that stayed may simply be the one that fit.
screen: `WHEN, NOT IF.` · `DONE QUIETLY.` · `MADE FOR MAN.` · `LET IT DWELL IN YOU.` · then, large: `WHAT STAYED.`

segments.voice: Count the six on your fingers, slowly: prayer, sabbath, scripture, giving, fasting, song. At each one, notice whether it still lives in your week, even in a small form, and fold a finger down for each that stayed. Then rest with the one that stayed longest; if you pray, give thanks for it.
The practices. Prayer, sabbath, scripture, giving, fasting and song: not achievements, but habits that move in and stay.
Keep this: what stayed, or in Paul's word, what dwells in you. A week from the top, done.

howItsDone: Christians keep these practices in many forms: daily prayer, a day of rest, Bible reading, giving, seasons of fasting such as Lent, and singing in worship and at home.
